title: New Support SLA & Premium Queue Rollout — internal briefing (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad to shape the announcement & internal Q+A for the upcoming Support SLA changes and Premium Queue pilot. Keep this thin — want something we can copy into an HR/CS/Eng-ready announcement once we lock dates.

Audience: internal employees (CS, Eng, Product, SRE, Sales/AM) + selected beta customers (later). Primary internal ask: clarity on how routing/escalation changes affect engineers and oncall.

Planned headline (short):
- "Introducing Support SLA v2 and Premium Queue pilot — clearer SLAs, faster triage for paying customers"

One-liner for external customers (for reference):
- "We're rolling out v2 of our Support SLAs with a Premium Queue for committed customers — faster response and prioritized engineering escalation for critical incidents."

Draft internal announcement body (very rough):
- TL;DR: SLA v2 introduces a simpler severity ladder (P0/P1/P2), clarified MTTR targets, and a Premium Queue pilot for Reserved/Dedicated customers. Changes effective in phases starting Apr 6.
- Why: reduce confusion, improve predictability for paying customers, and align internal routing with capacity and billing tiers.
- What changes:
  - New severity definitions and expected response windows (see Confluence link)
  - Premium Queue: ticket tag + dedicated triage window (15 min SL for initial response) + fast-path to Eng oncall where needed
  - Escalation flow standardized (CS -> SRE -> Eng -> Exec for high-impact incidents)
  - Billing & refund language will be handled by finance/legal (not in this memo)

Key talking points for managers and oncall leads: (bullet-guide for channel replies)
- This is about clarity and speed. We expect fewer misrouted tickets and faster time-to-first-response for high-value customers.
- Premium Queue is an operational pilot: capacity limited initially. We will measure impact on latency and engineer context switching.
- Eng oncall won't be automatically paged for every Premium Queue ticket — only for tickets that match our P0/P1 criteria or after CS/SRE triage escalates.
- If you see increased load on SRE/eng during the pilot, flag it immediately to the rollout owners (Samir / Elena).

Proposed internal timeline (working):
- Mar 15–28: internal dry-run with CS + SRE (scripts + fake tickets)
- Apr 1: internal announcement to all staff (FYI + manager Q+A session Apr 2)
- Apr 6: pilot goes live for a small subset of Dedicated customers
- Apr 6–May 10: pilot measurement window; weekly health syncs
- May 15: decide next steps (expand, iterate, or pause)

Draft FAQ (internal-facing) — pull from CS prep notes:
Q: Who gets Premium Queue?
A: Initially a tiny set of Reserved/Dedicated customers we onboard into the pilot (billing + contract teams will pick).

Q: Will Eng oncall be paged more?
A: Not automatically. We tightened the triage gate: CS/SRE review first. Eng oncall gets engaged when severity criteria met or after SRE escalation.

Q: How do we tag a ticket as Premium?
A: Tickets will have a "premium=true" tag and route to a separate queue in Zendesk. Doc: Confluence link.

Q: What metrics are we tracking?
A: time-to-first-response, time-to-resolution, number of escalations to Eng, customer satisfaction for pilot cohort, and engineer context-switch count (via oncall notes).

Operational play: immediate steps for CS and Eng leads
- CS: update triage runbook; run two rehearsals (Mar 20, Mar 25) with SRE.
- SRE: create a short triage checklist for Premium tickets. Add one escalation point person per shift.
- Eng: review runbooks for P0/P1 criteria. Identify 2 engineers (per team) willing to be rapid-contact for escalations during pilot.

Slack channels / communication flows (draft):
- #support-premium (for pilot activity summaries, only invited)
- #support-escalations (existing) for live incidents
- Use ephemeral daily digest to avoid noise (Samir to set up digest bot)

Open questions / risks (working):
- Risk: enginee r fatigue if many borderline premium tickets are escalated. Mitigation: strict triage gate + weekly limits per team.
- Risk: customers expect immediate engineering changes; need clear expectations in CS replies.
- We need a short runbook for when Premium Queue capacity is exceeded (auto-degrade to standard queue + CS-owned updates).

TODO (short):
- [ ] Lock pilot customer list with Sales (Samir) — target by Mar 10 (STATUS: in progress)
- [ ] Finalize exact SLA windows and put in Confluence (Elena) — target Mar 12
- [ ] Draft customer-facing FAQ + email copy (Aisha) — target Mar 20
- [ ] Create internal manager Q+A slide (Noor) — target Mar 30
- [ ] Automation: Zendesk tag routing + digest setup (Infra/SRE) — target Mar 25 (PR #87)

Notes to self / scratch:
- Keep internal announcement short — 3 bullets + link to FAQ. Offer a manager-only sync the next day to answer role-specific questions.
- Be explicit about escalation thresholds; ambiguity will blow up oncall bandwidth.
- Collect a small set of sample tickets to use in the dry-run.

References / links to copy from: Confluence (Support SLA v2 draft), JIRA-3421 (routing infra work), PR-87 (zendesk routing), slack thread: #cs-pricing-discuss (thread ts=1700xxxx).

Last editorial thought: use "pilot" language heavily — sets expectation that we're testing and may iterate. Avoid promising scope expansion or refunds until legal says so.

Next actions for me (Noor): schedule manager Q+A, tidy this memo to 1-pager, upload customer FAQ draft to Confluence and ping Sales for pilot list.

-- end of scratchpad (will iterate after sync with Samir/Elena)
